about: Corrections to the international ledger (data/ledger/intl/). Each is applied last, over the merged rows, and never edits a source file. A correction names the source record it overrides, what it changes, and receipts; receipts with a `cache` path are string-checked against the cached page on every build (pipeline/build-intl.mjs). Schema: pipeline/docs/intl.md §Corrections.

corrections.reason: FIFA's report lists Danny Murphy (#4) as a starter, off 78', scoring England's second goal at 48+'. Murphy did not play. The line is Steven Gerrard's: he started, scored just before half-time and was replaced by Hargreaves. BBC's team line and post-match report name Gerrard; RSSSF's Gerrard log has the cap with a goal and has no Murphy log.

receipts.source: BBC Sport clockwatch (cited in the archive record's warning)

corrections.reason: UEFA's lineup page lists Bulgaria's #8, a starter who played the whole match, as 'Stoytcho Stoilov'. Wikidata's lineup for the match (Q115935574) has #8 as Hristo Stoichkov, captain, and RSSSF's Stoichkov log has this match as his cap 77. Stoycho Stoilov (Q932974) is a real, different player, so the name is not a transliteration. Two sources against one, both checked against the cached copies. The ledger already paired the UEFA line with Stoichkov's RSSSF cap; this correction records why, and keeps the entry from being linked to Stoilov.

corrections.reason: Latvia 0-2 Spain, Riga, Euro 2008 qualifying Group F (UEFA match 83726). RSSSF's Villa log (cap 22, goals cell blank, running total 10 before and after), Wikipedia's list of Villa's international goals and Wikidata (no goal for Villa, Q83006, in the match item) all give him nothing. UEFA's contemporary pages, captured two to twelve days after the match, credit him with the opener on 45': the scorer line and the goal event on the events page, and the match report's text ('Villa bundled in' Angulo's cross on the stroke of half-time; Xavi's 60' shot deflected in off Iniesta). martj42 and Wikipedia's Group F page agree with UEFA. Decided by the match report, not by count: RSSSF's log and Wikipedia's goal list are both one short, so Villa's ledger total is 60, not the widely cited 59. Why the national-team tallies omit it (an own goal by Zakresevskis, who challenged for the cross, in the federation's books?) is not verified.

receipts.source: UEFA.com events page, Latvia v Spain (match 83726), Wayback 20070608094241

corrections.reason: France 4-0 Netherlands, Saint-Denis, Euro 2024 qualifying. RSSSF's Griezmann log leaves the goals cell of cap 118 blank but its own running total rises 42 -> 43 on that row. Since 2026-10-22 the parser reads the goals column, never the running total, so the row is 0 with a cumulative_mismatch warning. Wikidata (goal at first half +2) and martj42 (2') both have his goal; the page's running total agrees with them. The blank cell is RSSSF's slip.
